title: STS shortcuts and their IntelliJ workflow equivalents
answer: STS is based on the Eclipse platform, so common STS/Eclipse shortcuts include Ctrl+Shift+R for Open Resource, Ctrl+Shift+T for Open Type, Ctrl+O for Quick Outline, F3 for Open Declaration, Ctrl+Shift+G for references, Ctrl+Space for content assist, Ctrl+1 for Quick Fix, Ctrl+Shift+F for formatting, and Alt+Shift+R for Rename. Exact bindings can vary by operating system or customized keymap. In this AeroTopo course the Java IDE is IntelliJ IDEA only, so the lesson demonstrates the equivalent navigation, completion, intention, formatting, and refactoring workflows in IntelliJ rather than switching the simulator to STS.

steps.title: Map STS Open Resource to IntelliJ Go to File
steps.question: STS uses Ctrl+Shift+R to open a resource by name; In IntelliJ, use Go to File on AeroTopoApplication.java and explain what is being indexed, why this works even when you do not know the package path, and how file-oriented navigation differs from class-oriented search in the next step.
steps.why: Both workflows solve the same developer problem: file-name-driven navigation. This course remains IntelliJ-only, so we demonstrate the equivalent action without switching IDEs.
steps.why_te: Go to File file peru meeda search chestundi; package tree manually expand cheyyalsina avasaram ledu; Ee step file-oriented navigation ni establish chestundi, class/type search next step lo separate ga compare chestam.

steps.title: Map STS Open Type to IntelliJ Go to Class
steps.question: STS uses Ctrl+Shift+T to find a Java type, while IntelliJ uses Go to Class; Search for AeroTopoApplication and explain why a type index is more precise than a file-name search when class names, nested types, or generated sources are involved, and when you would still prefer Go to File instead.
steps.why: Type-oriented navigation is different from raw file browsing because the IDE understands Java classes and packages. IntelliJ Go to Class provides that semantic navigation.
steps.why_te: Go to Class Java type index ni use chestundi; File search kanna idi class identity meeda focus chestundi; nested types leda type-name navigation kavali ante ee workflow more direct ga untundi.

steps.title: Map STS Quick Outline to IntelliJ File Structure
steps.question: STS Quick Outline and IntelliJ File Structure both navigate inside the file already open; Use AeroTopoApplication.java to explain how fields, constructors, and methods are indexed within one source file, why this is faster than global search for local navigation, and what problem it solves once a class grows beyond a few methods.
steps.why: The important skill is symbol-level movement inside one file rather than scrolling line by line. IntelliJ File Structure exposes the same conceptual navigation model.
steps.why_te: File Structure current source file lopala fields, constructors, methods list ni chupistundi; Global project search kaadu; already open class lo member ki fast ga jump cheyyadam ee step specific purpose.

steps.title: Map STS F3 declaration navigation to IntelliJ
steps.question: STS F3 and IntelliJ Go to Declaration follow a selected symbol to its definition; Trace SpringApplication.run from AeroTopoApplication and explain how declaration navigation uses the resolved symbol rather than matching text, why that matters with overloaded methods or same-named symbols, and how it helps inspect framework APIs safely.
steps.why: Declaration navigation lets a developer follow typed relationships through the codebase instead of searching manually for definitions.
steps.why_te: Go to Declaration selected symbol resolved definition ki teesukeltundi; Plain text search kanna symbol identity use chestundi, kabatti overloaded methods leda same-name references unna appudu correct declaration ni inspect cheyyachu.

steps.title: Map STS reference search to IntelliJ Find Usages
steps.question: STS Ctrl+Shift+G and IntelliJ Find Usages answer the opposite question from Go to Declaration: they show who depends on a symbol; Use AeroTopoApplication as the target and explain why reviewing callers and references before a rename or signature change reduces refactoring risk across a multi-file enterprise project.
steps.why: Usage discovery reduces the risk of changing a symbol without understanding its callers or references across the project.
steps.why_te: Find Usages declaration nundi reverse direction lo dependents ni chupistundi; Shared symbol refactor mundu callers ekkada unnayo chusi impact scope estimate cheyyadam ee step main engineering value.

steps.title: Map STS content assist to IntelliJ code completion
steps.question: STS content assist and IntelliJ code completion use the current type context to suggest legal APIs; Open completion at the shown location and explain how compile-time type information narrows the suggestions, why this reduces memorization and typing mistakes, and how completion differs from a quick fix that reacts to a diagnosed problem.
steps.why: Both features use code context to reduce memorization and typing errors while helping the developer discover available APIs.
steps.why_te: Code completion current type context batti available APIs suggest chestundi; Developer memory meeda depend kakunda valid methods discover cheyyachu; diagnostic problem fix cheyyadam next intention-action workflow responsibility.

steps.title: Map STS Quick Fix to IntelliJ intention actions
steps.question: STS Ctrl+1 Quick Fix and IntelliJ Alt+Enter are diagnostic-driven actions rather than general completion; Inspect the available intention actions and explain how the caret location and current inspection determine the offered fixes, why blindly accepting an action can still be risky, and when imports or exception fixes are appropriate.
steps.why: The available fix depends on the exact caret and diagnostic context rather than a generic menu.
steps.why_te: Alt+Enter current caret diagnostic ki context-specific intention actions istundi; Import, exception, refactor suggestions problem batti marutayi; completion laga general API list kaadu, kabatti action apply mundu reason check cheyyali.

steps.title: Map STS formatting to IntelliJ Reformat Code
steps.question: STS formatting and IntelliJ Reformat Code apply configured code-style rules without changing program semantics; Reformat AeroTopoApplication.java and explain why consistent whitespace and layout reduce noisy diffs, how team style settings matter, and why formatting should be separated conceptually from refactoring or functional code changes.
steps.why: Formatting is a team-consistency tool, not merely cosmetic. The IntelliJ action applies this project's configured style without switching IDEs.
steps.why_te: Reformat Code configured style rules ni apply chestundi, program behavior ni ; Consistent formatting valla team diffs logic changes meeda focus avutayi; functional refactor tho formatting ni mix cheyyakunda use cheyyadam better.

steps.title: Map STS Rename to IntelliJ safe refactoring
steps.question: STS Rename and IntelliJ safe Rename operate on symbol identity rather than raw text; Use the preview-only rename flow and explain how IDE usage analysis protects unrelated comments or same-text identifiers, why reviewing the preview is valuable before a project-wide change, and how semantic rename differs from Find Usages alone.
steps.why: Semantic rename uses the IDE symbol model and is safer than replacing matching text blindly across unrelated files or comments.
steps.why_te: Safe Rename symbol references ni IDE model tho update chestundi; Raw text replace kanna unrelated occurrences protect avutayi; preview chusi affected usages verify cheyyadam production refactor lo final safety check.

data.note: Equivalent workflow demonstration only; no AeroTopo production symbol is changed.
